title: Giant Rydberg Excitons Delineated as Relativistic Bound States
authors: Mitsuyoshi Takahata, Ikuko Akimoto, Nobuko Naka
abstract: We examined the energy-momentum relationship of the valence band of Cu$_2$O, which has gained interest as an emerging solid host for giant Rydberg states. Our findings reveal a nonparabolic dispersion, described using the rest mass (0.570 times the free electron mass) and rescaled light speed ($1.6\times 10^5$ m/s), which draws parallels with relativistic theory for high-energy particles. We propose a straightforward expression for the bound-state energies of Rydberg excitons with finite quantum defects, whose energy scheme deviates from the hydrogenic series. This formulation identifies relativistic kinematics as the physical origin of quantum defects, offering a streamlined basis for future studies on complex many-body correlations.
summary: This work analyzes the valence band of Cu2O, finding that its energy dispersion is nonparabolic and best described by relativistic physics. By incorporating this relativistic band structure into the exciton model using the Dirac equation, the authors successfully calculate and verify the binding energies of giant Rydberg excitons. This links solid-state band structure physics directly to highly excited atomic-like quantum phenomena.
main_problem: To investigate the relativistic nature of the hole energy dispersion in Cu2O and use this understanding to theoretically calculate the binding energies of giant Rydberg excitons.
main_result: The nonparabolic dispersion of the valence band is successfully modeled using relativistic kinematics, and the Dirac equation approach accurately predicts the binding energies of odd-parity Rydberg excitons.
method: The study combines time-resolved cyclotron resonance measurements to characterize the band dispersion with theoretical calculations employing the Dirac equation for exciton binding energies.
model_or_system: The system is the valence band of Cu2O, modeled using relativistic energy-momentum relations, and the exciton binding energies are calculated using a Dirac equation adapted for nonparabolic bands.
key_observables: Effective mass ($m_{CR}$), nonparabolicity parameter, exciton binding energies ($E_n$), and quantum defect values ($\delta_{n,\ell}$).
important_parameters: Rest mass (0.570 $m_e$), rescaled light speed ($1.6	imes 10^5$ m/s), and the energy gap ($E_g \approx 2172$ meV).
main_assumptions: The Dirac approach is used for binding energies, which is an isotropic approximation that neglects the spin exchange interaction for even-parity states.
figures_summary: Figures show the time-dependent and temperature-dependent effective mass relaxation, the band dispersion vs. wavenumber, and contour maps of time-resolved cyclotron resonance spectra.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from experimental characterization of the nonparabolic hole band dispersion via CR measurements, to deriving the relativistic dispersion relation, and finally applying the Dirac equation to calculate and compare exciton binding energies.
why_interesting: The explicit connection drawn between the relativistic kinematics governing the semiconductor band structure and the quantum defect in Rydberg excitons provides a powerful, unified theoretical framework for strongly interacting quasi-particles.
